stem.text: Let \( g(x) = 2 x^{3} - 12 x^{2} + 18 x \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether g has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = 3 \) and at \( x = -4 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = 3 \), g has a relative minimum because \( g'(3) = 0 \) and \( g''(3) = 12 > 0 \); at \( x = -4 \), g has no relative extremum because \( g'(-4) = 210 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( g'(x) = 6 x^{2} - 24 x + 18 \), which factors as \( g'(x) = 6 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right) \).
\( g'(3) = 0 \), so \( x = 3 \) is a critical point, while \( g'(-4) = 210 \ne 0 \), so \( x = -4 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test g has a relative minimum at \( x = 3 \). At \( x = -4 \) the first derivative is not zero, so g has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.
